    87	theorem moduleKSheaf_eq_toModuleKSheaf (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    88	    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    89	    C.left.moduleKSheaf k = Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C := by
    90	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom

    96	and the same structure sheaf (`moduleKSheaf_eq_toModuleKSheaf`); they differ only in the
    97	universe at which `Ext` is annotated, and `Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv` is a `k`-linear
    98	equivalence between those two annotations.  `finrank` does not distinguish linearly equivalent

   103	theorem ledgerGenus_eq_genus (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   104	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   105	    ledgerGenus C = genus C := by
   106	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
   107	  change Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)

     9	/-!
    10	# Degree slices of the relative-divisor functor + the degree-refined Abel map
    11	
    12	Campaign milestones **D1'** (degree-`d` divisor functor `DivFunctorDeg`, clopen
    13	degree decomposition, base-change stability of the fibre degree) and **A2**
    14	(degree-refined Abel map `abelDeg`) of the `instHasPicScheme` campaign
    15	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), on top of the landed divisor
    16	functor `Scheme.DivFunctor` (Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:div`;
    17	`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`).
    18	
    19	## The fibre degree
    20	
    21	For a family of relative effective divisors `x : DivFamily π T` (the quotient
    22	encoding: `q : O_{X_T} ↠ F = O_D` with invertible kernel ideal `I_D = ker q`),
    23	the **fibre degree** at `t : T` is
    24	
    25	  `x.fiberDeg t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
    26	
    27	Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`'s degree of the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` — the
    28	`H⁰`-only, cohomology-free rank.
    29	
    30	**AUDIT (encoding choice, D1').** The campaign phrase "rank-`d` of the
    31	finite-flat pushforward of `O_D`" is realized by its *pointwise shadow*: the
    32	in-tree substrate has no `q_* O_D`-as-locally-free-object (that is exactly the
    33	B3 rigid-pushforward engine, unbuilt), and for a finite flat family the rank of
    34	the pushforward at `t` *equals* `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t})` (pushforward along
    35	an affine morphism is exact and commutes with base change).  The fibre-section
    36	form is honest at full generality (any `π`, any `T`; `Module.finrank` junk
    37	value `0` if the fibre sections are infinite-dimensional, which does not occur
    38	for divisor fibres in the relative-curve regime) and is what Kleiman's
    39	`deg D_t` means.  When B3 lands, `q_* O_D` is locally free of rank
    40	`fiberDeg` and the two vocabularies fuse.
    41	
    42	**AUDIT (base change, D1').** `fiberDeg` is stable under arbitrary base change
    43	`ψ : T' ⟶ T` (`fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is
    44	the base change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t = ψ(t')` along the residue
    45	extension `κ(t) → κ(t')`, and `H⁰` of a finitely presented module with proper
    46	support commutes with base field extension (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`).  This is
    47	proved **axiom-clean** from the twist-free Γ-fibre core
    48	`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
    49	(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean`) — NOT from the twisted engine
    50	`Scheme.hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` (`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), which
    51	still rests on the sorried tensor–pullback leaf
    52	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso`.  At `m = 0` no twist is needed, so the
    53	degree lane stays sorry-free (recon correction to the campaign plan's
    54	"the 02KE/02KH engine is landed" — only its untwisted core is).
    55	
    56	## The clopen degree decomposition — honest form
    57	
    58	**AUDIT (coproduct pin, D1').** The naive presheaf-level statement
    59	"`DivFunctor = ⨿_d DivFunctorDeg d`" is FALSE: on a disconnected `T` a family
    60	with non-constant fibre degree lies in no degree piece, and at `T = ∅` every
    61	piece contains the (unique) empty family, so the pieces are not disjoint.  The
    62	honest pins delivered here are:
    63	
    64	* every `T`-point decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree pieces
    65	  (`DivFamily.degLocus`, `DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`,
    66	  `DivFamily.iSup_degLocus`, `DivFamily.degLocus_disjoint`) — this is the form
    67	  the coproduct assembly `G4` (`hom_sigma_decompose`) consumes;
    68	* on a nonempty preconnected `T` the canonical comparison
    69	  `Σ_d (DivFunctorDeg π d)(T) → DivFunctor π (T)` is a bijection
    70	  (`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective`);
    71	* degree pieces of a common class agree (`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`,
    72	  nonempty `T`).
    73	
    74	The only non-formal input is **Zariski-local constancy of the fibre degree**.
    75	This is TRUE in the campaign regime (relative curve: `D → T` is
    76	proper + quasi-finite, hence finite, and a finitely presented `T`-flat module
    77	with finite support has finite locally free pushforward — Mumford, *Abelian
    78	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) but is NOT derivable from the
    79	current in-tree substrate (it needs the finite/rank half of the B3 pushforward
    80	engine plus `D_t` finite from relative dimension 1).  Following the house gate
    81	pattern (`HasPicScheme`), it is pinned as the instance-free Prop-class
    82	`HasLocallyConstantDivDeg C` at the AJC curve regime, and every decomposition
    83	statement is ALSO provided in hypothesis-parametrized form (an explicit
    84	`IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so the eventual discharge is a
    85	one-line instance.  We deliberately do NOT state the gate for general `π`:
    86	for relative dimension `≥ 2` the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ` is
    87	locally constant), which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in
    88	general and by the degree only over curves.
    89	
    90	## The degree ledger and the Abel-map sign (A2)
    91	
    92	**Sign convention (audit item 7-half).** The Abel map is
    93	`abelMapWitness C = abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, i.e.
    94	
    95	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  —
    96	
    97	a divisor family maps to the *negative* of the class of its ideal sheaf
    98	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:461`).  The degree-refined Abel map
    99	`abelDeg C d : divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C` is the restriction of
   100	`abelMapWitness` along the degree-`d` inclusion; its defining property is
   101	`abelDeg_app_mk`.  It deliberately lands in `picSharp C` — carving out
   102	`picSharpDeg C d` is milestone B4, not this file.
   103	
   104	**AUDIT (degree-coherence vocabulary, A2).** "The ideal sheaf `ker q` of a
   105	rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" is stated in the **rank (colength)
   106	vocabulary** — the strongest honestly-provable form today: the χ-ledger
   107	(`deg = χ(I) − χ(O)`, campaign P3) is unbuilt, and the adelic
   108	`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor` degree cannot yet be attached to the sheaf-theoretic
   109	line bundle `ker q` on a family fibre (that needs the `M ≅ O(div s)`
   110	regular-section bricks, also P3).  What IS proved, per fibre `t`:
   111	
   112	* the ideal restricts to the fibre: the kernel–pullback comparison
   113	  `(I_D)_t ≅ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (`DivFamily.fiberKernelIso`) and the
   114	  fibre ideal inclusion `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` stays monic
   115	  (`DivFamily.mono_fiber_kernel_ι`) with `(I_D)_t` invertible
   116	  (`DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel`) — `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an honest
   117	  effective Cartier divisor (Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`);
   118	* its colength is the degree: `O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t ≅ (O_D)_t`
   119	  (`DivFamily.fiberCokernelIso`), so
   120	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = fiberDeg x t = d`
   121	  (`DivFamily.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel`,
   122	  `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel`).
   123	
   124	In χ-ledger terms this is exactly `deg_t(ker q) = χ(I_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −d`;
   125	the translation becomes a theorem once P3 lands.
   126	
   127	## References
   128	
   129	Blueprint: to be attached to the campaign's D1'/A2 nodes.

   148	/-! ## §0. Dimension transport for fibre section modules -/
   149	
   150	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   151	/-- **Transport of the fibre-section dimension along an isomorphism of fibre
   152	modules.**  An isomorphism of sheaves of modules on the scheme-theoretic fibre
   153	`π₀.fiber s` induces a `κ(s)`-linear equivalence on global sections
   154	(evaluation at `⊤` is functorial, and the `κ(s)`-scalar action factors through
   155	`Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap`), so the `κ(s)`-dimensions agree.  Twist-free
   156	sibling of `Scheme.hilbertFunction_eq_finrank_of_iso`
   157	(`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), serving the degree lane where no tensor
   158	operations may enter. -/
   159	lemma finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso {W B : Scheme.{u}} (π₀ : W ⟶ B) (s : B)
   160	    {G G' : (π₀.fiber s).Modules} (e : G ≅ G') :
   161	    (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
   162	     Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G, ⊤))
   163	      = (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
   164	         Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G', ⊤)) := by
   165	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
   166	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
   167	  have γe := ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules (π₀.fiber s) ⋙
   168	    PresheafOfModules.evaluation (π₀.fiber s).ringCatSheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)).mapIso
   169	      e).toLinearEquiv
   170	  exact LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
   171	    { toFun := γe
   172	      map_add' := γe.map_add
   173	      map_smul' := fun c x => γe.map_smul ((π₀.fiberResidueMap s).hom c) x
   174	      invFun := γe.symm
   175	      left_inv := γe.left_inv
   176	      right_inv := γe.right_inv }

   178	/-! ## §1. The fibre degree of a family of relative effective divisors -/
   179	
   180	namespace DivFamily
   181	
   182	variable {π : X ⟶ S}
   183	
   184	/-- The **fibre degree** of a family of relative effective divisors
   185	`x : DivFamily π T` at a point `t : T` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`):
   186	
   187	  `deg D_t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
   188	
   189	the `κ(t)`-dimension of the global sections of the restriction of the divisor
   190	structure sheaf `F = O_D` to the scheme-theoretic fibre `(X_T)_t`.  This is
   191	the pointwise shadow of "rank of the finite-flat pushforward `q_* O_D`" (equal
   192	to it whenever the pushforward exists as a locally free module, i.e. in the
   193	relative-curve regime once the B3 engine lands; see the module docstring
   194	audit).  `Module.finrank` junk value `0` in the infinite-dimensional case. -/
   195	noncomputable def fiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   196	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : ℕ :=
   197	  letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
   198	    ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F)
   199	  Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
   200	    Γ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F, ⊤)
   201	
   202	/-- **The fibre degree is well defined on divisor classes**: equivalent
   203	families (`DivFamily.Rel`, i.e. same divisor `ker q = ker q'`) have equal
   204	fibre degrees — the target isomorphism restricts to each fibre and transports
   205	the section dimension. -/
   206	theorem Rel.fiberDeg_eq {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
   207	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : x.fiberDeg t = y.fiberDeg t := by
   208	  obtain ⟨f, -⟩ := h
   209	  exact finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T.hom) t
   210	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).mapIso f)
   211	
   212	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   213	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   214	-- Heartbeat headroom: instantiating the Γ-fibre base-change core provisions
   215	-- pullback/pushforward and field instances under binders, as in the sibling
   216	-- engines of `QuotFunctorDef`.
   217	/-- **The fibre degree is stable under base change** (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`;
   218	Kleiman §3, functoriality of `Div`): for `ψ : T' ⟶ T` and `t' : T'` over
   219	`t := ψ(t')`, the fibre degree of the pulled-back family at `t'` equals the
   220	fibre degree of `x` at `t`.
   221	
   222	Route (all inputs axiom-clean): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is the base
   223	change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t` along `Spec κ(t') → Spec κ(t)`
   224	(`Scheme.isPullback_fiberBaseChange`, the `quotBaseSquare`/residue-field
   225	pasting); the two fibre restrictions of `F` are matched by pseudofunctor
   226	coherence (`Scheme.pullbackSquareIso`); proper support of `F/T` restricts to
   227	the fibre (`Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback` on Mathlib's fibre
   228	square); and the twist-free Γ-fibre flat base-change core
   229	`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
   230	(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean` — support descent `G ≅ i_* i^* G` + the
   231	CLOSED 02KE heart) transports the dimension across the residue extension.
   232	No tensor operations enter, so — unlike the twisted engine
   233	`hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` — this consumes no sorried leaf. -/
   234	theorem fiberDeg_pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) (x : DivFamily π T)
   235	    (t' : (T'.left : Scheme.{u})) :
   236	    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).fiberDeg t' = x.fiberDeg (ψ.left.base t') := by
   237	  haveI hFqc : x.F.IsQuasicoherent := letI := x.isFinitePresentation; inferInstance
   238	  haveI : ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F).IsQuasicoherent :=
   239	    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom _ x.F hFqc
   240	  have hpsFt : Modules.HasProperSupport
   241	      ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberToSpecResidueField (ψ.left.base t'))
   242	      ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F) :=
   243	    Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback
   244	      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   245	        (T.left.fromSpecResidueField (ψ.left.base t')))
   246	      x.F x.isFinitePresentation x.properSupport
   247	  have eF : (pullback.snd π T'.hom).fiberModule t'
   248	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).obj x.F)
   249	      ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (fiberBaseChange π ψ t')).obj
   250	          ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F) :=
   251	    pullbackSquareIso (fiberBaseChange_fiberι π ψ t').symm x.F
   252	  exact (finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T'.hom) t' eF).trans
   253	    (Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport
   254	      (Field.toIsField (T.left.residueField (ψ.left.base t')))
   255	      (Field.toIsField (T'.left.residueField t'))
   256	      (isPullback_fiberBaseChange π ψ t')
   257	      ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F) hpsFt)

   259	/-! ## §2. The fibre of the ideal sheaf — Cartier fibres and the degree ledger
   260	
   261	The `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` sign convention of the Abel map (module docstring) is
   262	anchored fibrewise: on every fibre `X_t` of the family, the ideal sheaf
   263	restricts to an honest invertible ideal `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` cutting out the
   264	fibre divisor `D_t`, and its colength `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t)` is
   265	exactly the fibre degree.  In χ-ledger terms (campaign P3, unbuilt):
   266	`deg_t(ker q) = χ((I_D)_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −deg D_t = −d` for a degree-`d`
   267	family. -/
   268	
   269	/-- **The kernel ideal restricts to an invertible ideal on every fibre**
   270	(Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`, specialised to the fibre inclusion):
   271	the kernel of the fibre restriction `q_t` of the quotient map is locally
   272	trivial of rank one.  Instantiation of the divisor base-change theorem
   273	`Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
   274	(`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`) at Mathlib's fibre square. -/
   275	theorem isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   276	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
   277	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (Limits.kernel
   278	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map x.q)) :=
   279	  Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial
   280	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   281	      (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)) x.q x.epi
   282	    (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
   283	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
   284	    x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
   285	
   286	/-- **The ideal inclusion stays monic on every fibre**: `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}`
   287	— the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is
   288	an invertible subsheaf, not merely an invertible quotient-kernel).  This is
   289	the flat-base-change monomorphism `Modules.mono_pullback_map_kernel_ι`
   290	(Stacks 00HL affine-locally) at the fibre square: `T`-flatness of `O_D` is
   291	what forbids the ideal from degenerating on special fibres. -/
   292	theorem mono_fiber_kernel_ι {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   293	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
   294	    Mono ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
   295	      (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)) :=
   296	  Modules.mono_pullback_map_kernel_ι
   297	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   298	      (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)) x.q x.epi
   299	    (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
   300	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
   301	    x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
   302	
   303	/-- **The fibre of the ideal is the ideal of the fibre**: the kernel–pullback
   304	comparison `(I_D)_t = (ker q)|_{X_t} ⟶ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (Kleiman
   305	§3: "Since `D` is `T`-flat, `p^* I` equals the ideal of `D_{T'}`", at
   306	`T' = Spec κ(t)`).  The `IsIso` witness is passed to `asIso` explicitly (the
   307	project `@asIso` idiom), so no instance search runs. -/
   308	noncomputable def fiberKernelIso {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   309	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
   310	    (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (Limits.kernel x.q)
   311	      ≅ Limits.kernel
   312	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map x.q) :=
   313	  @asIso _ _ _ _
   314	    (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t) x.q)
   315	    (Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison
   316	      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   317	        (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)) x.q x.epi
   318	      (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
   319	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
   320	      x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial)
   321	
   322	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   323	/-- **The fibre of the divisor structure sheaf is the cokernel of the fibre
   324	ideal inclusion**: `O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t ≅ (O_D)_t`.  In the abelian category
   325	`(X_T).Modules` the epimorphism `q` is the cokernel of its kernel
   326	(`ShortComplex.Exact.gIsCokernel`), and the module pullback along the fibre
   327	inclusion — a left adjoint (`Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`) —
   328	preserves the cokernel cofork.  Together with `fiberKernelIso` and
   329	`mono_fiber_kernel_ι` this realizes the fibre short exact sequence
   330	`0 → (I_D)_t → O_{X_t} → O_{D_t} → 0` of an effective Cartier divisor. -/
   331	noncomputable def fiberCokernelIso {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   332	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
   333	    Limits.cokernel
   334	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
   335	          (Limits.kernel.ι x.q))
   336	      ≅ (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F :=
   337	  haveI := x.epi
   338	  haveI : PreservesColimitsOfSize.{0, 0}
   339	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)) :=
   340	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   341	      ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).leftAdjoint_preservesColimits
   342	  haveI : Epi (((ShortComplex.mk (Limits.kernel.ι x.q) x.q
   343	      (Limits.kernel.condition x.q)).map
   344	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t))).g) :=
   345	    @CategoryTheory.Functor.map_epi _ _ _ _
   346	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)) inferInstance
   347	      _ _ x.q x.epi
   348	  ((colimit.isColimit _).coconePointUniqueUpToIso
   349	    (((CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.exact_kernel x.q).map_of_epi_of_preservesCokernel
   350	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)) x.epi
   351	      inferInstance).gIsCokernel))
   352	
   353	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   354	/-- **The degree ledger, rank vocabulary** (the A2 degree-coherence lemma, in
   355	the strongest honestly-provable form today — see the module docstring audit):
   356	the fibre degree of a divisor family is the **colength of its fibre ideal**,
   357	
   358	  `fiberDeg x t = dim_{κ(t)} Γ(X_t, coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}))`.
   359	
   360	In χ-ledger terms this is `deg_t(ker q) = χ((I_D)_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −fiberDeg x t`

     8	/-!
     9	# The divisor-level index bridge to the sibling χ-ledger (AJC.rr.principal)
    10	
    11	`RiemannRoch/CurveCoheight.lean` (ajc-rr) compares the two *point* index sets used for
    12	divisors on a curve:
    13	
    14	```
    15	X.PrimeDivisor  ≃  {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}
    16	```
    17	
    18	the right-hand side being the index set of the sibling project's `CurveDivisor`
    19	(`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, `RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean`), whose χ-ledger proves
    20	`deg (div g) = 0` sorry-free. This file lifts that comparison from points to **divisors and
    21	their degree**, which is the form the open leaf
    22	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` consumes:
    23	
    24	* `Scheme.WeilDivisor.addEquivNonGeneric` — `Div(X) ≃+ ({x // x ≠ η} →₀ ℤ)`, additively;
    25	* `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree_eq_sum_nonGeneric` — degree is the coefficient sum on **either**
    26	  index set, so the transport does not move degrees.
    27	
    28	## What this is and is not
    29	
    30	This is the *first* of the two carrier mismatches that `WeilDivisor.lean` lists as the cost of
    31	porting the sibling's χ-ledger conclusion. It is now closed, and the transport is additive, so
    32	it carries the degree homomorphism rather than only the underlying sets.
    33	
    34	It is **not** the port. The remaining mismatch is the residue-degree weighting of the
    35	sibling's `deg` (discharged over `k̄` by `Adelic.residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`, which
    36	sits downstream of `WeilDivisor.lean` — see the discussion at `principal_degree_zero`), and the
    37	χ-machinery itself still has to arrive. ajc-rr's staging audit (inbox I-0495, 2026-07-28)
    38	measured that port as near-mechanical: 22 cone files compile against AJC dependencies with
    39	byte-identical bodies.
    40	
    41	The coheight bound `∀ z, coheight z ≤ 1` is carried as a hypothesis exactly as in
    42	`CurveCoheight.lean`, and for the same reason: it *is* the curve hypothesis, so assuming it
    43	loses nothing, while proving it bottoms out in standard-smooth material that sits downstream
    44	of this file. Discharge it with `Adelic.coheight_le_one_of_curve` where that is in scope.
    45	-/
    46	
    47	set_option autoImplicit false
    48	
    49	universe u
    50	
    51	open CategoryTheory
    52	
    53	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    54	
    55	namespace Scheme.WeilDivisor
    56	
    57	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace X]
    58	
    59	/-- **The divisor-level index comparison, additively.** `Finsupp.domCongr` of ajc-rr's
    60	point-level `PrimeDivisor.equivNonGeneric`; additive because relabelling the index set of a
    61	finitely-supported function commutes with pointwise addition.
    62	
    63	Additivity is what makes this usable for a *degree* statement: `degree` is an
    64	`AddMonoidHom` (`degree_hom`), and a bare `Equiv` of divisor groups would not respect it. -/
    65	noncomputable def addEquivNonGeneric (hdim : ∀ z : X, Order.coheight z ≤ 1) :
    66	    X.WeilDivisor ≃+ ({x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ) :=
    67	  Finsupp.domCongr (Scheme.PrimeDivisor.equivNonGeneric hdim)
    68	
    69	/-- **Degree is the coefficient sum on either index set** — the transport moves no degrees.
    70	
    71	`degree` sums the bare coefficients (`Σ_Y D Y`), and relabelling along a bijection leaves a
    72	finite sum unchanged (`Finsupp.sum_mapDomain_index`, whose two side conditions are `rfl` here
    73	because the summand `fun _ n => n` ignores the index). So the sibling's degree-zero conclusion
    74	transports along `addEquivNonGeneric` without a correction term.
    75	
    76	This is the statement that makes the index mismatch *closed* rather than merely stated: an
    77	index equivalence that did not respect degree would not help the leaf. -/
    78	theorem degree_eq_sum_nonGeneric (hdim : ∀ z : X, Order.coheight z ≤ 1)
    79	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
    80	    degree D = (addEquivNonGeneric hdim D).sum (fun _ n => n) := by
    81	  change (D : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ).sum (fun _ n => n)
    82	    = (Finsupp.equivMapDomain (Scheme.PrimeDivisor.equivNonGeneric hdim)
    83	        (D : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ)).sum (fun _ n => n)
    84	  rw [Finsupp.equivMapDomain_eq_mapDomain,
    85	    Finsupp.sum_mapDomain_index (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ _ _ => rfl)]
    86	
    87	/-- The transported form of the degree-zero conclusion: a divisor whose relabelled
    88	coefficient sum vanishes has degree zero. The shape in which the sibling's `deg_divOf` will be
    89	consumed once its χ-machinery is ported. -/
    90	theorem degree_eq_zero_of_sum_nonGeneric_eq_zero (hdim : ∀ z : X, Order.coheight z ≤ 1)
    91	    {D : X.WeilDivisor}
    92	    (h : (addEquivNonGeneric hdim D).sum (fun _ n => n) = 0) :
    93	    degree D = 0 :=
    94	  (degree_eq_sum_nonGeneric hdim D).trans h
    95	
    96	end Scheme.WeilDivisor
    97	
    98	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# `G1` IS FREE AT THE CANONICAL ACTION: the invariance match, discharged
    10	
    11	`AJC.picrep.etale-rep.invariance`.
    12	
    13	## What this file removes
    14	
    15	`Picard/PicEtDescentGoal.lean` states the descent goal — a `k'`-side representation
    16	of `picEt (C_{k'})` plus a Galois quotient plus `hcov` plus a predicate match
    17	`IsInvariantMatch` yields `(picEt C).RepresentableBy Y` over `k` — and carries that
    18	match as an **explicit undischarged hypothesis**, identified there as what campaign
    19	`G1` owes.
    20	
    21	**At the canonical action it is not a hypothesis at all.** `isInvariantMatch_canonical`
    22	proves `IsInvariantMatch C rep (semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) T` for
    23	every test `T`, with **no hypothesis beyond `rep` and the curve's own binders**: no
    24	finiteness, no separability, no `IsGalois`, no rational point, no condition on the
    25	Galois group. So `G1` leaves this route, and the descent goal's inputs drop from four
    26	to three: `rep`, the Galois quotient, and `hcov`.
    27	
    28	## Why it is free — the reason, not just the fact
    29	
    30	The two predicates being matched are *not independent conditions on one object*.
    31	`IsInvariantMatch` asks that
    32	
    33	* `(rep.homEquiv.symm c).left` is **equivariant** for the action `ρ`, and
    34	* the transported class is **`Γ`-invariant** for the twist action on `picEt C`
    35	
    36	agree. At the canonical `ρ = semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep`, the
    37	`γ`-component of the action *is* `twistMor C rep γ`, which is **defined** by
    38	transporting the functor action `galoisActionPicEt` along `rep`. So both sides are
    39	images of one and the same functor-level statement, and the match is an identity
    40	rather than a coincidence. Three steps, each free:
    41	
    42	1. `isEquivariant_iff_galTwistMor` — equivariance of the underlying scheme map is the
    43	   same equation read in the slice over `Spec k'` (`Over.OverMorphism.ext` both ways).
    44	   `galTwistMor` is that slice packaging of `pullbackGalMap`, and it is the `k'`-side
    45	   partner of `PicEtGaloisBridge`'s `k`-slice `twistTest` — `twistTest T γ⁻¹` is
    46	   `pullbackGalMap … γ` on underlying schemes, which is *already* recorded as `rfl` at
    47	   `I-1455`, and `twistTest_eq_restrictTest_galTwistMor` is the slice-level form.
    48	2. `homEquiv_twist_comp` — applying `rep.homEquiv` to the square's right-hand side
    49	   gives `(galoisActionPicEt C γ).inv` applied to `rep.homEquiv φ`. This is
    50	   `homEquiv_twistMor` plus **naturality of the action at `φ.op`**, and it is the step
    51	   that makes the whole thing free: `twistMor` was built from that natural
    52	   transformation, so naturality is exactly what un-builds it.
    53	3. `crossBaseIso_galoisActionPicEt_inv` — transporting along `picEt_crossBaseIso`
    54	   turns the inverse action into `picEt C` applied to
    55	   `restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso`, whose components are the **identity** on
    56	   underlying schemes. Iso cancellation; the cross-base identification's own
    57	   `inv_hom_id_app`.
    58	
    59	Composing, equivariance at `γ` is invariance at `γ⁻¹`; quantifying over the group,
    60	which both predicates do, makes them equal. `Gal(k'/k)` is a group, so the
    61	reindexing `γ ↦ γ⁻¹` is a bijection and no hypothesis on it is needed.
    62	
    63	## What this does NOT do
    64	
    65	* It closes **no** `sorry`. `rep` is still the campaign's undischarged output, and
    66	  clause (1) field 1 of `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is witnessed for **no**
    67	  curve. This file is verified with that theorem as a `sorryAx` control.
    68	* The remaining two inputs of the descent goal are untouched: `IsGaloisQuotient` at a
    69	  glued non-affine `X'` (`pic-f`'s row) and `hcov` at a nontrivial Galois level
    70	  (`pic-a`'s row). Nothing here makes either cheaper.
    71	* It does **not** rescue the non-vacuity problem `PicEtDescentGoal.lean` records for
    72	  the *pair* `(hcov, IsInvariantMatch)`. It resolves that problem for the match by
    73	  removing it — a hypothesis that is never assumed cannot be vacuously satisfied —
    74	  but `hcov`'s only exhibited witness site still trivialises the conclusion, and that
    75	  half is unchanged.
    76	* It does **not** subsume `isInvariantMatch_of_subsingleton`. **An earlier revision of
    77	  this docstring said it did — "the degenerate case of a fact that holds at every
    78	  extension" — and that is false** (fresh-context audit). That lemma quantifies over an
    79	  **arbitrary** action `ρ`; `isInvariantMatch_canonical` **pins** `ρ` to the canonical
    80	  one. Refuted in one line: `isInvariantMatch_canonical rep T` offered against
    81	  `IsInvariantMatch C rep ρ T` for a bound `ρ` is a type mismatch. The two are
    82	  **incomparable** — this one is more general in the extension, strictly *less* general
    83	  in the action — and that incomparability is intrinsic to discharging a hypothesis by
    84	  *choosing* the object it quantified over. The older lemma is still **load-bearing** at
    85	  its only consumer: `representableBy_picEt_of_degenerate` takes an external `ρ` and
    86	  cannot route through this file without also pinning it.
    87	
    88	## "Free" does not mean "empty" — and that is measured, not assumed
    89	
    90	The natural misreading of this file is that `IsInvariantMatch` was never a real
    91	condition. **Measured, and it was.** Asserting that the two sides of `IsInvariantMatch`
    92	are *equal as propositions* at the canonical action — `IsEquivariant` of
    93	`(rep.homEquiv.symm c).left` against `IsGalInvariant` of the cross-base-transported
    94	class — and closing it by `rfl` **fails**: "not definitionally equal" (`lake env lean`,
    95	oleans rebuilt first per `I-1057`). Equivariance of a scheme map for a semilinear action
    96	and `Γ`-invariance of a `picEt`-class are distinct propositions about distinct objects.
    97	
    98	So `isInvariantMatch_canonical` is a theorem and not `P ↔ P` in a costume; what §2's
    99	three steps do is *identify* two genuinely different statements. "Free" here means **no
   100	hypothesis is needed**, because the identification follows from the *definition* of
   101	`twistMor` — not that there was nothing to prove. Had that `rfl` succeeded, the honest
   102	headline would have been "the `G1` match was never an obligation", and this file would be
   103	bookkeeping; it is recorded because the polarity of that probe is the whole difference.
   104	
   105	**And the removal is not a relocation either** — the other half of what a "four inputs
   106	became three" claim owes, since the natural failure is that the deleted hypothesis
   107	reappears inside a surviving one. Probed: state §4's *predecessor*'s full hypothesis list
   108	(`rep`, `hq`, `hcov`, `hmatch`, `hlft`) and close its conclusion by calling
   109	`seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch rep hq hcov hlft`, discarding `hmatch`. It
   110	elaborates, and the `unusedVariables` linter confirms `hmatch` is never referenced. So the
   111	new hypothesis set is *strictly* smaller — same `hq` at the same pinned action, nothing
   112	migrated into it, nothing hidden in an instance binder. Neither probe was implied by the
   113	green build; both were cheap.
   114	* Per `I-0491` there is no `HasRationalPoint` binder anywhere in this file.
   115	-/

   117	set_option autoImplicit false
   118	
   119	universe u
   120	
   121	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Limits Opposite
   122	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
   123	
   124	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   125	
   126	namespace Scheme
   127	
   128	namespace PicScheme
   129	
   130	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {k' : Type u} [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
   131	
   132	/-! ## §1. The `k'`-slice packaging of the base-change twist
   133	
   134	`FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`'s `pullbackGalMap` is a bare scheme map and
   135	`SemilinearGalAction.IsEquivariant` is stated about bare scheme maps, while `picEt`
   136	consumes slice morphisms. This section supplies the two bridges, both formal. -/
   137	
   138	/-- **The `γ`-twist of a base-changed test, in the slice over `Spec k'`.**
   139	
   140	Underlying map `pullbackGalMap k k' T.hom γ`; the slice condition is that map's own
   141	`pullbackGalMap_snd`, so it is a morphism *into* `baseTest T` **from its `γ`-twist* —
   142	which is the semilinearity, in the shape `twistMor` also has. -/
   143	noncomputable def galTwistMor (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k') :
   144	    (twistTestFunctor (k := k) γ).obj (baseTest (k' := k') T) ⟶ baseTest (k' := k') T :=
   145	  Over.homMk (pullbackGalMap k k' T.hom γ) (pullbackGalMap_snd k k' T.hom γ)
   146	
   147	@[simp] theorem galTwistMor_left (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k') :
   148	    (galTwistMor T γ).left = pullbackGalMap k k' T.hom γ := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- Every component of `restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso`'s **inverse** is the
   151	identity on underlying schemes, like its `hom` (`..._hom_app_left`). -/
   152	theorem restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso_inv_app_left (γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k')
   153	    (D : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))) :
   154	    ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).inv.app D).left = 𝟙 D.left := by
   155	  have h := congrArg Over.Hom.left
   156	    ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).hom_inv_id_app D)
   157	  rw [Over.comp_left, restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso_hom_app_left] at h
   158	  have hfixed : @Eq (D.left ⟶ D.left)
   159	      (𝟙 D.left ≫ ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).inv.app D).left)
   160	      (𝟙 D.left) := h
   161	  rw [Category.id_comp] at hfixed
   162	  exact hfixed
   163	
   164	/-- **The two spellings of the twist meet**: `PicEtGaloisBridge`'s `k`-slice
   165	`twistTest T γ⁻¹` is the identity-underlying comparison followed by the restriction
   166	of this file's `k'`-slice `galTwistMor T γ`.
   167	
   168	The inverse on one side is not a choice: `toSpecAut` acts by `Spec (γ⁻¹ • ·)`, so the
   169	`γ`-component of `pullbackGalMap` twists the base by `γ⁻¹`, and `I-1455` already
   170	records the underlying-scheme identity as `rfl`. This lemma is the slice form, which
   171	is what `picEt` can be applied to. -/
   172	theorem twistTest_eq_restrictTest_galTwistMor
   173	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k') :
   174	    twistTest (k' := k') T γ⁻¹
   175	      = (restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).inv.app (baseTest (k' := k') T)
   176	          ≫ (restrictTest k k').map (galTwistMor T γ) := by
   177	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   178	  rw [Over.comp_left, restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso_inv_app_left,
   179	    Over.map_map_left, galTwistMor_left]
   180	  have hfixed : @Eq (Limits.pullback T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k')
   181	      ⟶ Limits.pullback T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))
   182	      (𝟙 _ ≫ pullbackGalMap k k' T.hom γ) (pullbackGalMap k k' T.hom γ) :=
   183	    Category.id_comp _
   184	  exact hfixed.symm
   185	
   186	/-! ## §2. The three steps, each free -/
   187	
   188	section Steps
   189	
   190	variable {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
   191	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   192	  {X' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))}
   193	  (rep : (picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X')
   194	
   195	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   196	-- Heartbeat headroom: the `Over`/`pullback` coercion chain of `baseTest` unfolded
   197	-- against `IsEquivariant`'s bare-scheme spelling, as in `PicEtDescentGoal`'s §2b.
   198	/-- **Step 1: equivariance is a slice equation.**
   199	
   200	`SemilinearGalAction.IsEquivariant` at the canonical action unfolds to
   201	`pullbackGalMap … γ ≫ φ.left = φ.left ≫ (twistMor C rep γ).left` for each `γ`, and
   202	that is the underlying map of a square in the slice over `Spec k'`. Both directions
   203	are `Over` extensionality — the slice condition carries no further content because
   204	both sides already lie over `Spec k'`. -/
   205	theorem isEquivariant_iff_galTwistMor (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   206	    (φ : baseTest (k' := k') T ⟶ X') :
   207	    (pullbackSemilinearGalAction k k' T.hom).IsEquivariant
   208	        (semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) φ.left
   209	      ↔ ∀ γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k',
   210	          galTwistMor T γ ≫ φ
   211	            = (twistTestFunctor (k := k) γ).map φ ≫ twistMor C rep γ := by
   212	  constructor
   213	  · intro h γ; exact Over.OverMorphism.ext (h γ)
   214	  · intro h γ; exact congrArg Over.Hom.left (h γ)
   215	
   216	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   217	-- Heartbeat headroom: the `Over`/`pullback`/`baseTest` coercion chain is unfolded
   218	-- repeatedly against `IsEquivariant`'s and `picEt`'s differing spellings of one
   219	-- object, as in `PicEtDescentGoal.lean`'s §2b. Not a slow proof: each is a rewrite
   220	-- chain, but elaborating the statement costs the default budget on its own.
   221	/-- **Step 2, the step that makes `G1` free: the square's right-hand side is the
   222	functor action.**
   223	
   224	`rep.homEquiv` of `(twistTestFunctor γ).map φ ≫ twistMor C rep γ` is
   225	`(galoisActionPicEt C γ).inv` applied to `rep.homEquiv φ`.
   226	
   227	`twistMor` is *defined* as `rep.homEquiv.symm` of the action at the universal class,
   228	so `homEquiv_twistMor` returns that class, `rep.homEquiv_comp` moves the
   229	precomposition to `picEt`, and **naturality of `(galoisActionPicEt C γ).inv` at
   230	`φ.op`** slides the action past it. No geometry, and nothing about `C` beyond its
   231	binders: the content is that the twist at the representing object was built from a
   232	natural transformation. -/
   233	theorem homEquiv_twist_comp (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   234	    (φ : baseTest (k' := k') T ⟶ X') (γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k') :
   235	    rep.homEquiv ((twistTestFunctor (k := k) γ).map φ ≫ twistMor C rep γ)
   236	      = (galoisActionPicEt C γ).inv.app (op (baseTest (k' := k') T))
   237	          (rep.homEquiv φ) := by
   238	  have hnat := NatTrans.naturality_apply (galoisActionPicEt C γ).inv φ.op
   239	    (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 X'))
   240	  rw [rep.homEquiv_comp, homEquiv_twistMor, rep.homEquiv_eq φ]
   241	  exact hnat.symm
   242	
   243	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   244	-- Heartbeat headroom: the `Over`/`pullback`/`baseTest` coercion chain is unfolded
   245	-- repeatedly against `IsEquivariant`'s and `picEt`'s differing spellings of one
   246	-- object, as in `PicEtDescentGoal.lean`'s §2b. Not a slow proof: each is a rewrite
   247	-- chain, but elaborating the statement costs the default budget on its own.
   248	/-- **Step 3: the inverse action, transported across the cross-base identification,
   249	is `picEt C` applied to an identity-underlying comparison.**
   250	
   251	`galoisActionPicEt` is `galoisActionRestricted` conjugated by `picEt_crossBaseIso`, so
   252	transporting back cancels one conjugation (`Iso.inv_hom_id_app`) and leaves the
   253	restricted action, which `galoisActionRestricted_inv_app` computes as `picEt C` applied
   254	to `restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso`. -/
   255	theorem crossBaseIso_galoisActionPicEt_inv (D : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k')))
   256	    (γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k')
   257	    (c : (picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).obj (op D)) :
   258	    (picEt_crossBaseIso C k').hom.app (op ((twistTestFunctor (k := k) γ).obj D))
   259	        ((galoisActionPicEt C γ).inv.app (op D) c)
   260	      = (picEt C).map ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).hom.app D).op
   261	          ((picEt_crossBaseIso C k').hom.app (op D) c) := by
   262	  rw [galoisActionPicEt_inv_app_apply, galoisActionRestricted_inv_app,
   263	    ← CategoryTheory.comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id_app]
   264	  rfl
   265	
   266	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   267	-- Heartbeat headroom: the `Over`/`pullback`/`baseTest` coercion chain is unfolded
   268	-- repeatedly against `IsEquivariant`'s and `picEt`'s differing spellings of one
   269	-- object, as in `PicEtDescentGoal.lean`'s §2b. Not a slow proof: each is a rewrite
   270	-- chain, but elaborating the statement costs the default budget on its own.
   271	/-- **Precomposing with the identity-underlying comparison is injective on classes,
   272	and cancels.** Both directions of the final iff are this lemma; it is stated once
   273	rather than inlined twice because the two orientations of `Iso.hom_inv_id_app` are
   274	easy to get backwards. -/
   275	theorem picEt_map_comparison_eq_iff (D : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k')))
   276	    (γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k')
   277	    (x y : (picEt C).obj (op ((restrictTest k k').obj D))) :
   278	    (picEt C).map ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).hom.app D).op x
   279	        = (picEt C).map
   280	            ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).hom.app D).op y
   281	      ↔ x = y := by
   282	  have hcancel : ∀ z : (picEt C).obj (op ((restrictTest k k').obj D)),
   283	      (picEt C).map ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).inv.app D).op
   284	          ((picEt C).map
   285	            ((restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso (k := k) γ).hom.app D).op z) = z := by
   286	    intro z
   287	    rw [← CategoryTheory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp,

     9	/-!
    10	# The six-term cohomology slice of a short exact sequence of sheaves
    11	
    12	For a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0` of sheaves of `R`-modules on a small
    13	site, this file packages — **once, and elementwise** — the degree-`≤ 1` slice of the long
    14	exact cohomology sequence
    15	
    16	    0 → H⁰X₁ → H⁰X₂ → H⁰X₃ →δ→ H¹X₁ → H¹X₂ → H¹X₃
    17	
    18	obtained from mathlib's covariant `Ext`-sequence for the cohomology carrier
    19	`Sheaf.HModule = Ext(constModuleSheaf, ·)`: the connecting map `HModule.delta`, the four
    20	`Function.Exact` facts, injectivity at the left end and surjectivity of `H¹X₁ → H¹X₂`
    21	when `H¹X₃` vanishes.
    22	
    23	On top of the slice sit the two consumers of the χ-ledger:
    24	
    25	* **finiteness transfer** (`HModule.moduleFinite_middle`, `moduleFinite_left_zero`,
    26	  `moduleFinite_left_succ`): dimension bookkeeping between the terms of the sequence,
    27	  via the division-ring extension lemma `FiniteDimensional.of_exact`;
    28	* **additivity of χ** (`Sheaf.chi_eq_add_of_shortExact`): when `H¹X₃ = 0` and the five
    29	  remaining modules are finite, `χ X₂ = χ X₁ + χ X₃` — the alternating-sum identity
    30	  `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_alt_sum_eq_zero_of_exact₅` applied to the slice.
    31	
    32	The transports from mathlib's `(mk₀ f).postcomp`-spelling to `HModule.map` are definitional
    33	(`Ext`-postcomposition on both sides); each slot of the slice is nevertheless a named
    34	lemma, so downstream files never re-derive the sequence inline.
    35	-/
    36	
    37	set_option autoImplicit false
    38	
    39	universe u
    40	
    41	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    42	
    43	section FiniteDimensional
    44	
    45	variable {K V₁ V₂ V₃ : Type*} [DivisionRing K]
    46	  [AddCommGroup V₁] [Module K V₁] [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module K V₂]
    47	  [AddCommGroup V₃] [Module K V₃]
    48	
    49	/-- **Extension lemma for finite dimensionality.** If `V₁ → V₂ → V₃` is exact at `V₂` and
    50	the outer terms are finite-dimensional, so is the middle: the kernel of `V₂ → V₃` is the
    51	image of the finite `V₁`, and the coimage embeds into the finite `V₃`. (Mathlib's
    52	`Module.Finite.of_exact` asks for surjectivity of the second map; over a division ring the
    53	corestriction to the range removes that hypothesis.) -/
    54	theorem FiniteDimensional.of_exact (f : V₁ →ₗ[K] V₂) (g : V₂ →ₗ[K] V₃)
    55	    (h : Function.Exact f g) [FiniteDimensional K V₁] [FiniteDimensional K V₃] :
    56	    FiniteDimensional K V₂ := by
    57	  have hexact : Function.Exact f g.rangeRestrict := fun y => by
    58	    rw [← h y]
    59	    exact ⟨fun hy => congrArg Subtype.val hy, fun hy => Subtype.ext hy⟩
    60	  exact Module.Finite.of_exact hexact g.surjective_rangeRestrict
    61	
    62	end FiniteDimensional

    64	namespace CategoryTheory.Sheaf
    65	
    66	variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    67	  {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    68	  {S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R))}
    69	
    70	namespace HModule
    71	
    72	/-- **The connecting homomorphism** `δ : Hⁿ⁰(X₃) →ₗ[R] Hⁿ¹(X₁)` (`n₀ + 1 = n₁`) of a short
    73	exact sequence of sheaves of `R`-modules: postcomposition with the extension class of the
    74	sequence. -/
    75	noncomputable def delta (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
    76	    HModule S.X₃ n₀ →ₗ[R] HModule S.X₁ n₁ :=
    77	  hS.extClass.postcompOfLinear R (constModuleSheaf J R) h
    78	
    79	/-- Exactness of `Hⁿ(X₁) → Hⁿ(X₂) → Hⁿ(X₃)` at `Hⁿ(X₂)`, elementwise
    80	(`Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂'` transported to `HModule.map`). -/
    81	theorem exact_map_f_map_g (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ) :
    82	    Function.Exact (map S.f n) (map S.g n) := by
    83	  have h := Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂' (constModuleSheaf J R) hS n
    84	  rw [ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact] at h
    85	  exact h
    86	
    87	/-- Exactness of `Hⁿ⁰(X₂) → Hⁿ⁰(X₃) →δ→ Hⁿ¹(X₁)` at `Hⁿ⁰(X₃)`, elementwise
    88	(`Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₃'` transported to `HModule.map`/`HModule.delta`). -/
    89	theorem exact_map_g_delta (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
    90	    Function.Exact (map S.g n₀) (delta hS h) := by
    91	  have h' := Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₃' (constModuleSheaf J R) hS n₀ n₁ h
    92	  rw [ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact] at h'
    93	  exact h'
    94	
    95	/-- Exactness of `Hⁿ⁰(X₃) →δ→ Hⁿ¹(X₁) → Hⁿ¹(X₂)` at `Hⁿ¹(X₁)`, elementwise
    96	(`Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁'` transported to `HModule.map`/`HModule.delta`). -/
    97	theorem exact_delta_map_f (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
    98	    Function.Exact (delta hS h) (map S.f n₁) := by
    99	  have h' := Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁' (constModuleSheaf J R) hS n₀ n₁ h
   100	  rw [ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact] at h'
   101	  exact h'
   102	
   103	/-- **Left end of the slice**: `H⁰(X₁) → H⁰(X₂)` is injective when `X₁ ⟶ X₂` is a
   104	monomorphism (mathlib's `Abelian.Ext.postcomp_mk₀_injective_of_mono`). -/
   105	theorem injective_map_f_zero (hS : S.ShortExact) :
   106	    Function.Injective (map S.f 0) :=
   107	  haveI := hS.mono_f
   108	  Abelian.Ext.postcomp_mk₀_injective_of_mono (constModuleSheaf J R) S.f
   109	
   110	/-- **Right end of the slice**: `Hⁿ(X₁) → Hⁿ(X₂)` is surjective when `Hⁿ(X₃)` vanishes
   111	(exactness at `Hⁿ(X₂)` plus triviality of the next term). -/
   112	theorem surjective_map_f (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ) [Subsingleton (HModule S.X₃ n)] :
   113	    Function.Surjective (map S.f n) := fun y =>
   114	  (exact_map_f_map_g hS n y).mp (Subsingleton.elim _ 0)

   116	section FinitenessTransfer
   117	
   118	variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   119	  {R : Type u} [Field R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
   120	  {S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R))}
   121	
   122	/-- **Finiteness of the middle cohomology**: if `Hⁿ(X₁)` and `Hⁿ(X₃)` are finite, so is
   123	`Hⁿ(X₂)` (extension lemma along the exact slice). -/
   124	theorem moduleFinite_middle (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ)
   125	    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ n)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ n)] :
   126	    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ n) :=
   127	  FiniteDimensional.of_exact (map S.f n) (map S.g n) (exact_map_f_map_g hS n)

   130	finiteness descends. -/
   131	theorem moduleFinite_left_zero (hS : S.ShortExact) [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ 0)] :
   132	    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ 0) :=
   133	  FiniteDimensional.of_injective (map S.f 0) (injective_map_f_zero hS)
   134	
   135	/-- **Finiteness of the left cohomology in positive degree**: `Hⁿ¹(X₁)` is an extension of
   136	a submodule of the finite `Hⁿ¹(X₂)` by the image of the finite `Hⁿ⁰(X₃)` (exactness of the
   137	slice at `Hⁿ¹(X₁)`). -/
   138	theorem moduleFinite_left_succ (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁)
   139	    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ n₀)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ n₁)] :
   140	    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ n₁) :=
   141	  FiniteDimensional.of_exact (delta hS h) (map S.f n₁) (exact_delta_map_f hS h)

   149	variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}

   153	/-- **Additivity of the Euler characteristic** along a short exact sequence of sheaves of
   154	`R`-modules whose third term has vanishing `H¹`: `χ X₂ = χ X₁ + χ X₃`. This is the
   155	alternating-sum identity for the five-term exact slice

   157	theorem chi_eq_add_of_shortExact (hS : S.ShortExact)

    94	/-! ## §1. Line bundles on a product
    95	
    96	A *line bundle* on the relative curve `C ×_S T` is an invertible
    97	`O_(C ×_S T)`-module, i.e. a sheaf of modules locally free of rank one. In
    98	Mathlib `b80f227` the `Scheme.Modules` category is in place
    99	(`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf`), but there is no `IsInvertible`
   100	predicate on its objects yet (the closest is `Module.Invertible R M` for rings,
   101	in `Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`). iter-187 supplies the missing
   102	predicate as a project-side definition via local trivialisation on an affine
   103	open cover (see `IsLocallyTrivial` below), and refines `OnProduct` to the
   104	corresponding subtype.
   105	
   106	Blueprint reference: `def:line_bundle_on_product` (Kleiman §2, "absolute Picard
   107	functor"; Stacks tag 01HK). -/
   108	
   109	/-- A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `M` is **locally trivial of rank one** if every
   110	point `x : X` has an affine open neighbourhood `U` on which the restriction
   111	`M|_U` is isomorphic to the structure sheaf-as-module `𝒪_U`. This is the
   112	project-side stand-in for the missing Mathlib `IsInvertible` predicate on
   113	`Scheme.Modules`: line bundles (invertible sheaves) are exactly the
   114	`IsLocallyTrivial` modules, by Stacks tag 01HK / Hartshorne II §6. Local
   115	trivialisability is the structural content that survives base change along
   116	`f : Y ⟶ X` (Stacks 01HH) and is the source of the invertibility-preservation
   117	step for `pullbackAlongProjection`.
   118	
   119	The witness is bundled as `Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)`:
   120	the existence of a sheaf-of-modules isomorphism over the affine chart. -/
   121	def IsLocallyTrivial {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
   122	  ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧
   123	    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf)
   124	
   125	/-- The type of **line bundles on the product** `C ×_S T`: invertible sheaves of
   126	`O_(C ×_S T)`-modules, where the product is the categorical pullback of the
   127	projections `πC : C ⟶ S` and `πT : T ⟶ S`. In Kleiman's notation with `X = C`
   128	and base `S`, this is `Pic_C(T) = Pic(C ×_S T)`, the value of the absolute
   129	Picard functor at `T`.
   130	
   131	iter-187: refined to the subtype of `(Limits.pullback πC πT).Modules` cut out
   132	by the project-side predicate `IsLocallyTrivial` (locally trivial of rank one).
   133	The carrier is now genuinely the line-bundle subobject of `Scheme.Modules`,
   134	matching the blueprint statement `def:line_bundle_on_product`. Iter-186's
   135	all-modules carrier is recovered by forgetting the second component. -/
   136	def OnProduct {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) : Type (u+1) :=
   137	  { M : (Limits.pullback πC πT).Modules // IsLocallyTrivial M }
   138	
   139	/-- Projection from a line bundle on the product to its underlying
   140	sheaf of modules. -/
   141	abbrev OnProduct.carrier {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   142	    (L : OnProduct πC πT) : (Limits.pullback πC πT).Modules := L.1
   143	
   144	/-- A line bundle on the product is locally trivial of rank one. -/
   145	lemma OnProduct.isLocallyTrivial {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
   146	    (L : OnProduct πC πT) : IsLocallyTrivial L.carrier := L.2
   147	
   148	/-- **Stacks 01HH (pullback of an invertible sheaf is invertible).** For any
   149	morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ X` and any locally-trivial sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules
   150	`M`, the pulled-back module `f^* M : Y.Modules` is again locally trivial.
   151	
   152	The proof unfolds an affine open cover trivialising `M`, pulls back along `f`,
   153	and observes that `f^*` commutes with restriction along open immersions (the
   154	`pullback`/`restrictFunctor` natural isomorphism in
   155	`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf`) so that the trivialising chart for
   156	`M|_U` becomes a trivialising chart for `(f^* M)|_(f⁻¹ U)`. The full chart-chase
   157	involves the natural-isomorphism `restrictFunctorIsoPullback` plus the
   158	preservation of `SheafOfModules.unit` under pullback (Mathlib
   159	`Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.PullbackFree`'s
   160	`unitToPushforwardObjUnit`). The chart-chase is complete and the lemma is
   161	proved below. -/
   162	lemma IsLocallyTrivial.pullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) {M : X.Modules}
   163	    (hM : IsLocallyTrivial M) :
   164	    IsLocallyTrivial ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M) := by
   165	  intro y
   166	  obtain ⟨U, hxU, hU_aff, eM⟩ := hM (f.base y)
   167	  have hyU' : y ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ U := hxU
   168	  obtain ⟨V, hV_aff, hyV, hVU⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset hyU'
   169	  refine ⟨V, hyV, hV_aff, ?_⟩
   170	  -- Stacks 01HH chart-chase: factor `V.ι ≫ f` through `U` using
   171	  -- `Scheme.Hom.resLE`, then transport through `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`
   172	  -- and `pullbackComp` to identify the pullback at `V` with the pullback of
   173	  -- the unit on `U` to `V`. Close via `eM` and `pullbackObjUnitToUnit`
   174	  -- (which is an iso since `Opens.map g.base` is final via the
   175	  -- `RepresentablyFlat` instance).
   176	  obtain ⟨eM⟩ := eM
   177	  set g : (V : Scheme) ⟶ (U : Scheme) := f.resLE U V hVU with hg_def
   178	  have hg_comp : g ≫ U.ι = V.ι ≫ f := Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι f hVU
   179	  haveI : (TopologicalSpace.Opens.map g.base).Final :=
   180	    CategoryTheory.final_of_representablyFlat _
   181	  refine ⟨?_⟩
   182	  -- 1: ((pullback f).obj M).restrict V.ι ≅ (pullback V.ι).obj ((pullback f).obj M)
   183	  let i1 :=
   184	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback V.ι).app ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M)
   185	  -- 2: ≅ (pullback (V.ι ≫ f)).obj M
   186	  let i2 := (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp V.ι f).app M
   187	  -- 3: ≅ (pullback (g ≫ U.ι)).obj M  (using V.ι ≫ f = g ≫ U.ι)
   188	  let i3 := (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr hg_comp.symm).app M
   189	  -- 4: ≅ (pullback g).obj ((pullback U.ι).obj M)
   190	  let i4 := ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g U.ι).symm).app M
   191	  -- 5: ≅ (pullback g).obj (M.restrict U.ι)
   192	  let i5 := (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).mapIso
   193	    ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback U.ι).symm.app M)
   194	  -- 6: ≅ (pullback g).obj (unit_U)
   195	  let i6 := (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).mapIso eM
   196	  -- 7: ≅ unit_V  (pullback of unit is unit via the Mathlib morphism, which is
   197	  -- iso since the underlying `Opens.map g.base` is Final)
   198	  let i7 := asIso (SheafOfModules.pullbackObjUnitToUnit g.toRingCatSheafHom)
   199	  exact i1 ≪≫ i2 ≪≫ i3 ≪≫ i4 ≪≫ i5 ≪≫ i6 ≪≫ i7

   201	/-! ## §2. The pullback functor along the projection
   202	
   203	For a morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ Z` and an invertible `O_Z`-module `M`, the
   204	pullback `f^* M` is an invertible `O_Y`-module (the pullback of an
   205	open-cover-trivialisation of `M` trivialises `f^* M`, and the pullback of a free
   206	module of rank one is free of rank one — Stacks tag 01HH). Specialising to the
   207	projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT : C ×_S T ⟶ T` gives the pullback map
   208	`π_T^* : Pic(T) → Pic(C ×_S T)`. Mathlib's underlying `Scheme.Modules.pullback`
   209	functor (in `Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf`) supplies the pullback on
   210	the full category of sheaves of modules; iter-175+ will restrict it to
   211	invertible sheaves once the `OnProduct` carrier is unpacked.
   212	
   213	Blueprint reference: `def:pullback_along_projection` (Kleiman §2; Stacks tag
   214	01HH). -/
   215	
   216	/-- **Pullback along the projection** `π_T : C ×_S T ⟶ T` of a relative
   217	curve. Sends a *line bundle on `T`* — i.e. an `O_T`-module `N` equipped with a
   218	proof `hN : IsLocallyTrivial N` — to the line bundle `π_T^* N` on `C ×_S T`,
   219	induced by the `Scheme.Modules.pullback` functor on `Scheme.Modules` together
   220	with the preservation step `IsLocallyTrivial.pullback` (Stacks 01HH).
   221	
   222	iter-187: refined to consume the `OnProduct`-style subtype on the source: the
   223	underlying carrier is the direct application of Mathlib's
   224	`Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT)` functor at `N`, and the
   225	locally-trivial witness comes from the project-side helper
   226	`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback` (Stacks 01HH), which is proved. -/
   227	noncomputable def pullbackAlongProjection {S C T : Scheme.{u}}
   228	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) (N : T.Modules) (hN : IsLocallyTrivial N) :
   229	    OnProduct πC πT :=
   230	  ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).obj N,
   231	    hN.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)⟩
   232	
   233	/-! ## §3. Composition of pullbacks
   234	
   235	The composition law for line-bundle pullback (Stacks tag 01HG) says that for any
   236	composable morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y, g : Y ⟶ Z` and any line bundle `M ∈ Pic(Z)`,
   237	the natural isomorphism `(g ∘ f)^* M ≅ f^* g^* M` makes the pullback functor
   238	into a (pseudo-)functor `Sch^op ⥤ Cat`.
   239	
   240	Specialised to the relative curve setting: given `g : T' ⟶ T` over `S`, the
   241	base-change morphism `g_C := id_C ×_S g : C ×_S T' ⟶ C ×_S T` satisfies
   242	`π_T ∘ g_C = g ∘ π_{T'}` (definition of the fiber product). Therefore on
   243	line bundles `g_C^* ∘ π_T^* = π_{T'}^* ∘ g^*`, with the equality realised as the
   244	canonical natural isomorphism of pullback functors via the pseudo-functoriality
   245	of `Scheme.Modules.pullback` (Mathlib `Modules.pullbackComp`).
   246	
   247	Blueprint reference: `lem:pullback_compose` (Kleiman §2; Stacks tag 01HG). -/
   248	
   249	/-- **Composition of line-bundle pullbacks** along the projection. For a base
   250	scheme `S`, a curve-side morphism `πC : C ⟶ S`, test objects `T, T'` over `S`
   251	via `πT : T ⟶ S` and `πT' : T' ⟶ S`, and a morphism `g : T' ⟶ T` over `S`
   252	(encoded by the hypothesis `πT' = g ≫ πT`), set
   253	`g_C := id_C ×_S g : C ×_S T' ⟶ C ×_S T`
   254	(the base-change morphism, given by `pullback.map`). On the underlying
   255	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` functors the two routes through the canonical
   256	naturality square give canonically isomorphic objects:
   257	```
   258	            Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT)
   259	  T.Modules  ─────────────────────────────────────────────►  (C ×_S T).Modules
   260	       │                                                              │
   261	       │ Scheme.Modules.pullback g            Scheme.Modules.pullback g_C
   262	       ▼                                                              ▼
   263	 T'.Modules  ─────────────────────────────────────────────►  (C ×_S T').Modules
   264	            Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT')
   265	```
   266	i.e. for any `N : T.Modules`,
   267	```
   268	(Modules.pullback g_C).obj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT)).obj N)
   269	  ≅
   270	(Modules.pullback (pullback.snd πC πT')).obj ((Modules.pullback g).obj N).
   271	```
   272	
   273	This natural isomorphism is the substantive content of the
   274	"line-bundle pullback functor is well-behaved under composition" fact
   275	(Stacks tag 01HG). At the level of the `OnProduct` carrier (which is a typed
   276	`sorry` in iter-174; see §1) it descends to equality of isomorphism classes
   277	`[g_C^* π_T^* N] = [π_{T'}^* g^* N] ∈ OnProduct πC πT'`.
   278	
   279	iter-186: closed via the chain
   280	1. `Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g_C (pullback.snd πC πT)` (functor iso applied at `N`)
   281	2. `Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr` for the equation `g_C ≫ snd πC πT = snd πC πT' ≫ g`
   282	   (`pullback.lift_snd` on the `pullback.map` lift).
   283	3. `(Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (pullback.snd πC πT') g).symm` (applied at `N`). -/
   284	theorem pullback_pullback_eq {S C T T' : Scheme.{u}}
   285	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) (πT' : T' ⟶ S) (g : T' ⟶ T)
   286	    (hg : πT' = g ≫ πT) (N : T.Modules) :
   287	    Nonempty
   288	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
   289	            (Limits.pullback.map πC πT' πC πT (𝟙 C) g (𝟙 S)
   290	              (by rw [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]) (by rw [Category.comp_id, hg]))).obj
   291	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).obj N) ≅
   292	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT')).obj
   293	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj N)) := by
   294	  set g_C : Limits.pullback πC πT' ⟶ Limits.pullback πC πT :=
   295	    Limits.pullback.map πC πT' πC πT (𝟙 C) g (𝟙 S)
   296	      (by rw [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]) (by rw [Category.comp_id, hg])
   297	  have key : g_C ≫ Limits.pullback.snd πC πT = Limits.pullback.snd πC πT' ≫ g :=
   298	    Limits.pullback.lift_snd _ _ _
   299	  refine ⟨?_⟩
   300	  refine (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g_C (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).app N ≪≫ ?_
   301	  refine (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr key).app N ≪≫ ?_
   302	  exact ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT') g).app N).symm
   303

   308	/-! ## §4. The relative Picard quotient (set-valued)
   309	
   310	The relative Picard presheaf `Pic^♯_{C/S}(T) := Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`
   311	quotients the line-bundle group of the product by the subgroup pulled back from
   312	the base. As a quotient of abelian groups it is a quotient set; equivalently,
   313	the equivalence relation `L ~ L' ↔ L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)` is captured by a
   314	`Setoid` on the line-bundle type `OnProduct πC πT`. The quotient
   315	`Quotient (preimage_subgroup πC πT)` is the underlying set of the relative
   316	Picard presheaf at `T`.
   317	
   318	The "preimage_subgroup" name follows the Kleiman/Stacks convention: the
   319	quotient is by the preimage `π_T^* Pic(T) ⊆ Pic(C ×_S T)`, treated as a
   320	subgroup (image of a group homomorphism); the project-side Lean encoding
   321	extracts the *Setoid* that the quotient construction takes.
   322	
   323	Blueprint reference: `thm:relative_pic_quotient_well_defined` (Kleiman §2,
   324	Def. `df:Pfs`). -/
   325	
   326	/-- **Well-definedness of the relative Picard quotient as a `Setoid`.**
   327	
   328	The equivalence relation on `OnProduct πC πT` defining the relative Picard
   329	presheaf
   330	```
   331	Pic^♯_{C/S}(T) := Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)
   332	```
   333	is the relation `L ~ L' ↔ L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)`. This relation is reflexive
   334	(`L ⊗ L⁻¹ = O_(C ×_S T) = π_T^* O_T ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)`), symmetric (the inverse of
   335	a line bundle in `π_T^* Pic(T)` is in `π_T^* Pic(T)`), and transitive
   336	(`L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)` and `L' ⊗ L''⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)` give
   337	`L ⊗ L''⁻¹ ∈ π_T^* Pic(T)`); hence is an equivalence relation, encoded by a
   338	`Setoid` on `OnProduct πC πT`.
   339	
   340	The substantive content is the well-definedness of the quotient: the canonical
   341	projection `OnProduct πC πT → Quotient (preimage_subgroup πC πT)` is the
   342	set-theoretic underlying map of the relative Picard presheaf at `T`.
   343	
   344	iter-186: with `OnProduct := (pullback πC πT).Modules`, the carrier is the
   345	modules category. We encode the **iso-class setoid** `L ~ L' ↔ Nonempty (L ≅ L')`.
   346	This is a substantive simplification: it identifies isomorphic modules
   347	(giving the underlying set of `Pic(C ×_S T)` once invertibility is imposed),
   348	but does not yet quotient by the pullback subgroup `π_T^* Pic(T)`. The full
   349	quotient requires a tensor-product structure on `Scheme.Modules` (Mathlib
   350	ships `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` but no monoidal structure on
   351	`Scheme.Modules` directly at `b80f227`) plus an inverse for invertibles;
   352	iter-187+: refine to `L ~ L' ↔ ∃ N : T.Modules, Nonempty (L ⊗ L'⁻¹ ≅
   353	pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N)` once both are available. -/
   354	noncomputable def preimage_subgroup {S C T : Scheme.{u}}
   355	    (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) :
   356	    Setoid (LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) where
   357	  r L L' := Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)
   358	  iseqv :=

events.text: The most promising real bridge is now concrete: for a divisor family \(D\) on \(C\times T\), prove on every residue-field fibre that the normalized Euler index of its ideal line bundle is \(-\deg(D_t)\). This would turn the existing colength statement into the arbitrary-test Abel degree pin, rather than adding another wrapper. I’m checking whether the current curve/cohomology instances discharge every finiteness and \(H^1\)-vanishing premise before I expose that as the Round 5 edit target.

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.Divisor

     8	/-!
     9	# The sheaf `𝒪(D)` associated to a Weil divisor on a curve
    10	
    11	For the curve bundle `X`, integral and smooth of relative dimension one over a field `K`, and a
    12	Weil divisor `D : X.CurveDivisor`, this file constructs the sheaf of `K`-modules `𝒪(D)` whose
    13	sections over an open `U` are the rational functions with poles bounded by `D` on `U`:
    14	
    15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.functionFieldOverAlgebraMap` / `functionFieldOverModule`: the
    16	  `K`-structure on the function field `K(X)` through the structure morphism, mirroring
    17	  `Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap` (deliberately *not* a global instance).
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.divisorSections`: the `K`-submodule of `K(X)` of sections of `𝒪(D)`
    19	  over `U`, and `Scheme.divisorSheaf`: the resulting sheaf of `K`-modules on the small Zariski
    20	  site of `X`.
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.divisorSheafLE`: the monomorphism of sheaves `𝒪(D) ↪ 𝒪(D')` induced
    22	  by `D ≤ D'`.
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.divisorSheafZeroIso`: the identification `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X` of the
    24	  divisor sheaf of the zero divisor with the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `K`-modules).
    25	
    26	## Sign convention
    27	
    28	For `g : K(X)` and a closed point `x`, "the pole order of `g` at `x` is bounded by `D x`" reads
    29	`ord_x g ≤ ofAdd (D x)` in `ℤᵐ⁰ = WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)`: a uniformizer has valuation
    30	`ofAdd (-1) < 1`, `g = 0` has valuation `0 = ⊥`, and at `D = 0` the bound is `≤ 1`, i.e. "`g`
    31	lies in the valuation subring at every closed point", which is exactly the statement identifying
    32	`𝒪(0)` with `𝒪_X`.
    33	
    34	## The empty-open corner
    35	
    36	The empty sieve covers `⊥` in `Opens.grothendieckTopology`, so a sheaf must have terminal (zero)
    37	sections over `⊥`. The naive predicate "`∀ x ∈ U, ord_x g ≤ …`" is *vacuously* all of `K(X)` over
    38	`⊥`, hence is *not* a sheaf. We therefore guard the definition: `divisorSections D U` is the naive
    39	bounded submodule when `U` is nonempty and `⊥` (the zero submodule) when `U` is empty, sealed
    40	behind `divisorSections_of_nonempty` / `divisorSections_of_empty`.
    41	-/
    42	
    43	set_option autoImplicit false
    44	
    45	universe u
    46	
    47	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    48	
    49	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    50	
    51	/-- The `K`-algebra structure map on the function field `K(X)` of a scheme over `Spec K`, through
    52	the structure morphism: `K →+* Γ(X, ⊤) →+* K(X)` (the germ at the generic point of a global
    53	section). Deliberately *not* a global `Algebra` instance, mirroring `Scheme.overModule`. -/
    54	noncomputable def Scheme.functionFieldOverAlgebraMap (K : Type u) [Field K] (X : Scheme.{u})
    55	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X] : K →+* X.functionField :=
    56	  (X.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint X) trivial).hom.comp (X.overAlgebraMap K ⊤)
    57	
    58	/-- The `K`-module structure on the function field `K(X)`, by restriction of scalars along
    59	`Scheme.functionFieldOverAlgebraMap`. Activate with `attribute [local instance]` where needed. -/
    60	@[reducible] noncomputable def Scheme.functionFieldOverModule (K : Type u) [Field K]
    61	    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X] :
    62	    Module K X.functionField :=
    63	  (Scheme.functionFieldOverAlgebraMap K X).toModule
    64	
    65	attribute [local instance] Scheme.functionFieldOverModule Scheme.overModule
    66	
    67	namespace Scheme
    68	
    69	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    70	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    71	
    72	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] in
    73	lemma functionFieldOverModule_smul_def (r : K) (g : X.functionField) :
    74	    r • g = Scheme.functionFieldOverAlgebraMap K X r * g := rfl
    75	
    76	/-- **The order of an integral element is nonnegative.** The order valuation at a closed point of
    77	the image in `K(X)` of any element of the stalk `𝒪_{X,x}` is `≤ 1`: integral elements have no
    78	pole. This is the heart of the `𝒪(D)`-submodule property and of the `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X` identification. -/
    79	lemma ord_algebraMap_stalk_le_one {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)
    80	    (y : X.presheaf.stalk x) :
    81	    Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx
    82	        (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) X.functionField y) ≤ 1 := by
    83	  letI := isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx
    84	  letI := isDedekindDomain_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx

    86	
    87	/-- **The `K`-structure map lands in every valuation subring.** The image of `r : K` in `K(X)`
    88	is the germ at the generic point of a global section; its germ at any closed point `x` realises
    89	it as an element of `𝒪_{X,x}`, hence it has no pole there: `ord_x (r · 1) ≤ 1`. -/
    90	lemma ord_functionFieldOverAlgebraMap_le_one {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (r : K) :
    91	    Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx (functionFieldOverAlgebraMap K X r) ≤ 1 := by
    92	  set t : Γ(X, ⊤) := X.overAlgebraMap K ⊤ r with ht
    93	  have hspec : genericPoint X ⤳ x := (genericPoint_spec X).specializes trivial
    94	  have hcomp := X.presheaf.germ_stalkSpecializes (U := ⊤) (y := x) trivial hspec
    95	  have happ := DFunLike.congr_fun (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom hcomp) t
    96	  rw [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply] at happ
    97	  have hrw : functionFieldOverAlgebraMap K X r
    98	      = algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) X.functionField
    99	          ((X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom t) := happ.symm
   100	  rw [hrw]
   101	  exact ord_algebraMap_stalk_le_one K hx _
   102	
   103	/-- The valuation upper bound imposed by a divisor `D` at a closed point `x`, in `ℤᵐ⁰`.
   104	The pole order of `g` at `x` is bounded by `D` iff `ord_x g ≤ divisorBound D hx`. -/
   105	noncomputable def divisorBound (D : X.CurveDivisor) {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
   106	    WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
   107	  letI D' : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ := D
   108	  ((Multiplicative.ofAdd (D' ⟨x, hx⟩) : Multiplicative ℤ) : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ))
   109	
   110	@[simp] lemma divisorBound_zero {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
   111	    divisorBound (0 : X.CurveDivisor) hx = 1 := by
   112	  rw [divisorBound]; rfl
   113	
   114	lemma divisorBound_mono {D D' : X.CurveDivisor} (h : D ≤ D') {x : X}
   115	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) : divisorBound D hx ≤ divisorBound D' hx := by
   116	  simp only [divisorBound, WithZero.coe_le_coe, Multiplicative.ofAdd_le]
   117	  exact (Finsupp.le_def.mp h) ⟨x, hx⟩
   118	
   119	/-- The **naive bounded submodule**: rational functions `g : K(X)` whose pole order at every
   120	closed point of `U` is bounded by `D`. Over `⊥` this is (vacuously) all of `K(X)`; the
   121	sheaf-correct `divisorSections` guards the empty open. -/
   122	noncomputable def boundedSections (D : X.CurveDivisor) (U : X.Opens) :
   123	    Submodule K X.functionField where
   124	  carrier := {g | ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X), x ∈ U →
   125	    Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx g ≤ divisorBound D hx}
   126	  zero_mem' := fun _ _ _ => by rw [map_zero]; exact zero_le
   127	  add_mem' := fun {g₁ g₂} h₁ h₂ x hx hxU =>
   128	    le_trans (Valuation.map_add _ g₁ g₂) (max_le (h₁ x hx hxU) (h₂ x hx hxU))
   129	  smul_mem' := fun r g hg x hx hxU => by
   130	    rw [functionFieldOverModule_smul_def, map_mul]
   131	    calc Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx (functionFieldOverAlgebraMap K X r)
   132	            * Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx g
   133	        ≤ 1 * Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx g := by
   134	          gcongr; exact ord_functionFieldOverAlgebraMap_le_one K hx r
   135	      _ = Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx g := one_mul _
   136	      _ ≤ _ := hg x hx hxU
   137	
   138	lemma mem_boundedSections {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U : X.Opens} {g : X.functionField} :
   139	    g ∈ boundedSections K D U ↔ ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X), x ∈ U →
   140	      Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx g ≤ divisorBound D hx :=
   141	  Iff.rfl
   142	
   143	/-- Sections over a larger open satisfy more constraints: `boundedSections` is antitone in `U`. -/
   144	lemma boundedSections_le_of_le {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
   145	    boundedSections K D U ≤ boundedSections K D V :=
   146	  fun _ hg x hx hxV => hg x hx (h hxV)
   147	
   148	/-- `boundedSections` is monotone in the divisor. -/
   149	lemma boundedSections_mono {D D' : X.CurveDivisor} (h : D ≤ D') (U : X.Opens) :
   150	    boundedSections K D U ≤ boundedSections K D' U :=
   151	  fun _ hg x hx hxU => le_trans (hg x hx hxU) (divisorBound_mono h hx)
   152	
   153	/-- **Sections of `𝒪(D)` over `U`.** The bounded submodule for nonempty `U`, and the zero
   154	submodule over the empty open — the guard forced by the sheaf condition at `⊥` (see the module
   155	docstring). -/
   156	noncomputable def divisorSections (D : X.CurveDivisor) (U : X.Opens) :
   157	    Submodule K X.functionField :=
   158	  ⨆ (_ : (U : Set X).Nonempty), boundedSections K D U
   159	
   160	lemma divisorSections_of_nonempty {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U : X.Opens}
   161	    (hU : (U : Set X).Nonempty) : divisorSections K D U = boundedSections K D U :=
   162	  iSup_pos hU
   163	
   164	@[simp] lemma divisorSections_of_empty {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U : X.Opens}
   165	    (hU : ¬ (U : Set X).Nonempty) : divisorSections K D U = ⊥ :=
   166	  iSup_neg hU
   167	
   168	lemma divisorSections_subsingleton_of_empty {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U : X.Opens}
   169	    (hU : ¬ (U : Set X).Nonempty) : Subsingleton (divisorSections K D U) := by
   170	  rw [divisorSections_of_empty K hU]; infer_instance
   171	
   172	/-- Membership in `𝒪(D)(U)` for a nonempty open: bounded pole orders at every closed point. -/
   173	lemma mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U : X.Opens}
   174	    (hU : (U : Set X).Nonempty) {g : X.functionField} :
   175	    g ∈ divisorSections K D U ↔ ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X), x ∈ U →
   176	      Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hx g ≤ divisorBound D hx := by
   177	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hU]; exact mem_boundedSections K
   178	
   179	/-- Sections over a larger open satisfy more constraints: `divisorSections` is antitone in `U`
   180	(for nonempty targets). -/
   181	lemma divisorSections_antitone {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U)
   182	    (hV : (V : Set X).Nonempty) : divisorSections K D U ≤ divisorSections K D V := by
   183	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K (hV.mono h), divisorSections_of_nonempty K hV]

   185	
   186	open Classical in
   187	/-- **Restriction of `𝒪(D)`-sections** along `V ≤ U`: the inclusion when `V` is nonempty
   188	(restriction only relaxes the pole bounds), the zero map into the terminal sections when `V`

   190	noncomputable def divisorSectionsRes (D : X.CurveDivisor) {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
   191	    divisorSections K D U →ₗ[K] divisorSections K D V :=

   194	lemma divisorSectionsRes_coe {D : X.CurveDivisor} {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U)

   212	  by_cases hW : (W : Set X).Nonempty
   213	  · have hV : (V : Set X).Nonempty := hW.mono hWV
   214	    apply Subtype.ext

   219	
   220	/-- The presheaf `U ↦ 𝒪(D)(U)` of `K`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
   221	noncomputable def divisorPresheaf (D : X.CurveDivisor) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} K where
